title: Menu, panel and picker become one overlay with one outcome type
body:
`State` holds `menu: Option<Menu>`, `panel: Option<Panel>`, `picker: Option<Picker>` and `picker_tick: Option<RegistrationToken>`, the last alive only while the picker is. Each overlay has its own outcome type: `menu::Outcome { Open, Close, Run(Action) }`, `PanelOutcome { Open, Close, Changed }` and `picker::Outcome { Open, Close, Show, New, CloseWorkspace, Move }`. `Open` and `Close` appear three times and `CloseWorkspace` twice. In `compositor.rs`:

- `run_key` routes `Key::Menu` to the picker, then the panel, then the menu, in an order nothing states.
- "is any overlay open" is written at the input gate and again for the scrim in `render`.
- teardown clears all three by hand.
- each of the five `Outcome::Run(Action::..)` arms begins with `self.menu = None`.
- "open the palette at New workspace" is written in `frame_hit` and in `picker_outcome`.
- the picker's inputs are rebuilt at every call: `ids: Vec<u32>` is collected at three sites, `Grid` built at three, and `cell_height` passed to `close_button` and `press` though `Grid::new` already had it.
- `paint_picker`, 139 lines, draws the picker's chrome in the compositor while `Menu::draw` and `Panel::draw` draw their own; `Picker.selected`, `confirming` and `dragging` are `pub` only for it.

The three fields can all be `Some` at once; see the bug "The palette opens over the settings panel and both stay open".

## Proposal

`overlay: Option<Overlay>` with `enum Overlay { Menu(Menu), Panel(Panel), Picker { picker, tick } }`. Each overlay's `key`, `press`, `release` and `motion` return one `Outcome { Open, Close, Run(Action) }`, with `Action` taking the picker's `Show`, `New` and `Move` and the panel's `Changed`. One `act` in the compositor closes the overlay and dispatches. `Picker::draw(over, under, &Grid, labels)` moves into `picker.rs` and the compositor keeps the thumbnail loop. `Grid` stores its button side and the picker methods take `&Grid`.

## Cost

About 80 lines in `compositor.rs` plus the three overlay modules, net about 30 fewer. The menu-over-panel state becomes unrepresentable.
close_reason: State holds overlay: Option<Overlay>, the three overlays return menu::Outcome, and Picker::draw lives in picker.rs, in 781975d. The note above covers the Run and Apply split.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/913b1d2c
notes.text: The proposal had one `act` that closes the overlay and then runs the action. Three actions keep the overlay open in the existing behaviour: a settings change keeps the panel, and a workspace closed or moved in the picker keeps the picker. The palette's Close workspace closes the palette. So `menu::Outcome` has two variants that carry an action. `Run(Action)` closes the overlay first, and `Apply(Action)` leaves it open. The picker's New became `Action::StartNewWorkspace`, its Show became `Action::ShowWorkspace`, its Move became `Action::MoveWorkspace`, and the panel's Changed became `Action::ChangeSettings(Settings)`.
